title: Shared shapes of the analysis artefacts — software-analysis capability
description: The definitions every companion schema of this capability refers to (software-analysis DEC-001 points 3 and 7, DEC-002 point 2, DEC-004 point 4): each artefact kind's id, the status an artefact carries, a line of text, and the id of a piece of evidence with the commit and the check it names. One home for each shape: the kinds' schemas (`actor`, `term`, `use-case`, `journey`, `quality-requirement`, `functional-requirement`, `constraint`, `domain-model-view`, `revalidation-record`) `$ref` them here, and the capability's commands read the id patterns from here, so the stamp that allocates an id and the check that judges one never disagree. The evidence point's companion (`revalidation-evidence`) is the one exception: a point's schema is compared across providers by its own file alone (COR-053 point 5), so it carries a copy of the artefact id, commit, check name and evidence id definitions, and a test holds the copy equal to these. Not a schema of any file itself.

slug.description: A word: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens — the word a stamp takes and the slug part of an actor's or a term's id.

status.description: Whether the artefact is in force. An artefact is withdrawn, never deleted: its file or entry stays, and its id is never used again (DEC-001 point 3).

actor-id.description: An actor's id: `ACT-` and a slug, stable across renames; the name of its file, `ACT-<slug>.md`, in the actors' folder.

actor-ref.description: An actor a use case, a journey or a requirement names: an actor of its own analysis by its id, or an actor of an analysis it builds on, named with that analysis by its component's name, such as `core:ACT-developer` (software-analysis DEC-001 points 2 and 4). Validation resolves the second against the actors the head of its analysis's glossary lists from that analysis.

term-id.description: A glossary term's id: `TERM-` and a slug, separate from the term's display name, so a rename breaks nothing that cites it; the key of its entry in the glossary.

builds-on.description: A glossary's head data: what its analysis takes from each analysis it builds on (software-analysis DEC-001 point 2), in the glossary's front matter as `builds-on`. A list, so the backbone never reads it as an entry of the collection. Each entry names the analysis by its component's name, the version its links name, the terms it takes, each by its id there and its name, and the actors it takes, each by its id there, its name, and the needs it brings to this analysis. No definition is copied. The head's text shows it, and the check holds the two equal.

analysis.description: The analysis it builds on, by its component's name.

version.description: The version of that analysis its links name: where its component declares the lowest version it needs, the floor (validation warns of another).

terms.description: The terms it takes, each listed by name with a link to its home.

actors.description: The actors it takes, each listed by name with a link to its home, and the needs it brings to this analysis: a need of the actor that only this analysis meets lives here.

use-case-id.description: A use case's id: `UC-` and its number within the project, independent of any grouping by area — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000 (`UC-007`), and no leading zero from 1000 on (`UC-1000`), so each number has one spelling and `UC-0007` is never a second id for `UC-007`.

journey-id.description: A journey's id: `JRN-` and its number within the project — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000, and no leading zero from 1000 on, so each number has one spelling.

requirement-id.description: A requirement's id, of any of the three kinds: `REQ-` and its number within the project, one numbering across quality requirements, functional requirements and constraints, so a requirement moved to another kind keeps it (software-analysis DEC-002 point 2). Three digits, zero-padded, below 1000, and no leading zero from 1000 on, as a use case's, so each number has one spelling.

view-id.description: A domain-model view's id: `VIEW-` and the slug its file's name gives after its number and the hyphen, so a view given another number keeps its id (software-analysis DEC-004 point 4).

artefact-id.description: The id of any analysis artefact.

commit.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal name in lower case: 40 digits under SHA-1, 64 under SHA-256. An abbreviated name is refused, so a commit has one spelling and a citation matches an entry exactly.

check-name.description: The name of an executed check: lower-case words of letters, digits and hyphens, joined by dots, the first beginning with a letter (`pytest-bridge.test-run.test-sandbox`). Underscores, slashes, colons and capitals are refused, so a test's name is slugged to fit; the name stands after the `#` of an evidence id.

evidence-id.description: The id of an entry of the evidence point, `pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence` (DEC-001 point 7): the artefact, the commit and the check the result is for, `<artefact>@<commit>#<check>` — an artefact id as above, then a commit's full name, then a check's name. A pattern cannot refer to another, so this one spells the six id shapes, the commit and the check name again, here beside them; a test holds them in step.
